title: NDSystem
description: An nD grammar's contextual coordinate system document (spec/SPEC.md §9), ported field-for-field from versum src/versum/nd.py NDSystem/AxisSpec (see src/five_d_nd/contract.py nd_system_violations()/axis_violations()). This $id resolves once the repository is published; until then, resolve schema $refs from a local copy (see tests/test_conformance.py's _local_validator()). validation.unknown_values is NOT constrained here: in versum, that check lives at the descriptor layer (grammar-descriptor.schema.json), not inside NDSystem itself. Accepts EITHER the bare NDSystem fields directly, OR a {"nd_system": {...}} wrapper around them, matching versum's own unwrap-FIRST semantics (`root = raw.get("nd_system", raw)`, src/versum/nd.py `NDSystem.from_dict`) via an if/then/else keyed on whether the top-level 'nd_system' key is present: if present, ONLY its value is checked against the bare-fields shape (a bad wrapper value — junk, null, {} missing required fields — is INVALID even when the surrounding document ALSO happens to carry valid bare top-level fields, matching versum: a present 'nd_system' key always wins, the bare fields are never a fallback); if absent, the document ITSELF is checked directly. An earlier anyOf-based version of this schema incorrectly accepted {"nd_system": "junk", ...valid bare fields...} because the bare-fields branch of an anyOf matches independently of the other branch; this if/then/else closes that gap by construction (there is exactly one branch per case, never two to choose from). INTENTIONAL schema strictness beyond versum: versum's from_dict str()-coerces 'version' and _tuple()-coerces 'vocabulary' BEFORE validating, so it (and this schema's own code counterpart, src/five_d_nd/contract.py) accepts odd values such as version: [], [1], {}, {"a":1} or null (all stringify to a non-empty string) and vocabulary: 0 or {} (both coerce to a non-empty one-element tuple) — this schema deliberately does NOT accept those shapes (version is string|number|boolean only; vocabulary's scalar form is a string only), to avoid inviting a hand-authored document to write them even though versum would swallow them; see the documented exceptions in tests/test_conformance.py's _ND_SYSTEM_SCHEMA_INTENTIONALLY_STRICTER.

version.description: §9 explicit field type: version is a STRING, or a JSON NUMBER accepted via str() coercion (versum's own `str(root.get('version', ''))`, applied before validating — e.g. the JSON integer 1 stringifies to a non-empty, truthy '1'). A JSON BOOLEAN, null, array, or object is MALFORMED here, even though versum's own str() coercion would swallow all four (str(True) == 'True', str(None) == 'None', str([]) == '[]', str({}) == '{}', all non-empty and truthy) — src/five_d_nd/contract.py rejects all four explicitly too (a NAMED P2 class, _ND_SYSTEM_VERSUM_P2_MALFORMED), so schema and code now agree here; only versum itself remains more lenient. An EARLIER version of this schema field also accepted boolean, matching versum's own leniency at the time — this field now matches the explicit §9 table instead.

version_5d.description: Informative; not validated beyond being a string.

additionalProperties.description: A null/falsy axis value is versum's own leniency (`v or {}`) — treated as an empty (all-default) axis spec, never a violation by itself.

validation.description: versum's own NDSystem.from_dict does `validation = root.get("validation") or {}` — a FALSY non-mapping (null, 0, false, "", []) is replaced by `or {}` and so is ACCEPTED (equivalent to an absent/empty validation object), while a TRUTHY non-mapping (e.g. "x", [1]) is passed straight to `.get(...)`, which a str/list do not have, and CRASHES. This schema accepts the same shapes versum accepts (an object, OR any JSON-falsy value) and rejects everything else, matching src/five_d_nd/contract.py's own `validation_raw and not isinstance(validation_raw, Mapping)` guard exactly.

stringOrArrayOfStrings.description: versum's own _tuple() coercion: a bare string means the same as a one-element array; null means an empty array; this schema accepts both shapes rather than requiring the caller to pre-wrap a scalar. Used ONLY where §9 itself declares the field a list of STRINGS specifically (e.g. 'allowed_axes', which names other axes by their string id) — NOT for 'vocabulary', whose own declared type is a list of ANY scalar (see scalarOrArrayOfScalars below).

scalarOrArrayOfScalars.description: §9 P3 violation fixed: §9 declares 'vocabulary' as `[...] | scalar | null` — ANY JSON scalar, not only a string. versum's own AxisSpec.violations() never type-checks a vocabulary ENTRY against the axis's own value_type (that cross-check lives in a SEPARATE method, AxisSpec.validate_value(), which validates a DATA VALUE against an axis — never called from violations()/NDSystem.violations() itself, confirmed by reading versum's own src/versum/nd.py); so a typed closed vocabulary (value_type 'integer' with vocabulary [1,2,3], 'boolean' with [true,false], 'number' with [0.5,1.0]) is well-formed and code/versum both accept it — this schema must too. versum's own _tuple() coercion: a bare scalar means the same as a one-element array; null means an empty array.

vocabulary.description: A bare scalar is accepted even when it is the EMPTY STRING "" — axis_violations()'s own _tuple("") coercion yields a one-element tuple ("",), which is non-empty and therefore satisfies the closed-vocabulary-is-non-empty rule below, however odd that may read. Verified against real versum (origin/main e416c81): vocabulary="" with vocabulary_mode: closed validates. This schema intentionally does NOT require minLength on the string form, matching that leniency exactly rather than being stricter than the code/versum it is meant to describe. Items MAY be any JSON scalar (string/number/boolean), not only a string — see scalarOrArrayOfScalars's own description for why a typed vocabulary (e.g. value_type 'integer' with vocabulary [1,2,3]) is well-formed.

primitives.description: versum's own _tuple() coercion: a bare primitive name means the same as a one-element array; null means an empty array (no primitives declared — never itself a violation).

ontology.description: versum's own AxisSpec.from_dict does `ontology = raw.get("ontology") or {}` — a FALSY non-mapping (null, 0, false, "", []) is replaced by `or {}` and so is ACCEPTED (equivalent to no ontology given), while a TRUTHY non-mapping (a non-empty string/list, true, a nonzero number) reaches `ontology.get(...)` in versum and CRASHES with AttributeError there. This schema accepts the same shapes versum accepts (an object, OR any JSON-falsy value) and rejects everything else, matching src/five_d_nd/contract.py axis_violations()'s own `ontology_raw and not isinstance(ontology_raw, Mapping)` guard exactly (same pattern as 'validation', above). An earlier version of this field REQUIRED 'id' AND 'version' on ANY object value unconditionally — wrongly rejecting a well-formed {} or {"id": "o"} in 'open'/'closed' mode (where ontology is never even READ — mode must be 'external' before id/version matter at all, see the allOf clause below) and wrongly rejecting the FLAT ontology_id/ontology_version form on its own. 'id'/'version' are now OPTIONAL here, each typed as a string when present; the id+version requirement itself lives ONLY in the vocabulary_mode == 'external' allOf clause below, which is the one place code/versum actually enforce it.

allOf.description: versum's own default: vocabulary_mode is 'closed' iff the KEY 'vocabulary' is present at all (even an empty array OR an empty string) AND vocabulary_mode is itself absent — NOT only when vocabulary_mode is explicitly 'closed' (the clause above). This mirrors axis_violations()'s has_vocab_key logic exactly. The bare-scalar branch now also accepts number/boolean (e.g. vocabulary: 0) — §9's own coercion table says a bare SCALAR (any JSON scalar, not only a string) means a one-element list, so 0 is NOT a malformed shape here; _tuple(0) == (0,), non-empty, satisfying the closed-vocabulary-is-non-empty rule.

code/versum compute ontology_id/ontology_version INDEPENDENTLY of each other (`axis.get("ontology_id") or ontology.get("id") or ""` and the same pattern for version) — so a FLAT ontology_id may satisfy 'id' while a NESTED ontology.version satisfies 'version', or vice versa, not only the all-flat or all-nested forms. This if/then enumerates all four satisfying combinations explicitly, exactly as code and versum accept them.
